I'm checking whether I still need lookups, and I'm leaning toward submitting my position now. The motion is a Policy item needing 4 of 5 with Steward sitting, and I'm working out whether a quarterly statistics mandate falls under the Council's infrastructure or content authority.

Now I'm going through the privacy and enforceability problems in the motion. Art. II §5 is about data portability, not privacy, so the motion has miscited its anchor. Its drafting is also vague on who publishes, the quarterly cadence, small-cell suppression, and how "overturned" differs from "dismissed," especially for automatic cost-filter dismissals.

I'm working through the remaining drafting gaps in the motion: the mandate needs a named publisher, a quarterly cadence, a small-cell suppression threshold, and clear definitions separating overturned from dismissed. I'm also noting that the sibling proposal's fee figures conflict with the rule against appeals generating revenue, so those numbers shouldn't appear in the statistics.

I'm weighing the potential harms of the statistics: per-clause overturn rates could be read as Council error rates, and small counts could identify an appellant. Under the EU-law and GDPR angle, aggregate anonymized figures should be fine, but small cells carry re-identification risk, so suppression thresholds matter. I'm leaning toward a yes on the principle with amendments, though I'm weighing whether to defer, since the Council doesn't yet have a drafted specification.

I'm weighing whether to vote yes with conditions or defer, and I'm leaning toward defer, since the enforceability gaps in the text are the real issue. The fixes could be made by amendment at the sitting, so I'm checking whether the Council actually lacks any information it needs.

I'm settling on defer, since the Council needs the publisher, cadence, minimum cell size, and outcome categories spelled out before it can adopt a mandate like this. I'm also listing the open questions: whether dismissed flag groups count separately from judicial dismissals, how vetoed and floor-clamped referrals should be handled, whether the scope covers Tier 1 and 2 actions or only appeals, and whether the Art. II §5 privacy anchor gets replaced with Art. II §4 and Art. VIII §1.2. I'm also considering whether Art. IV §5's transparency list is a minimum rather than a complete list, which would bear on the Council's authority to require this.

Now I'm settling on how to phrase the position text as JSON with single quotes inside, keeping it fairly brief.

{"submission":"position","position":"Recusal: the Council found on the record that this item does not limit the Steward's powers, so the Steward sits and the Policy threshold applies (4 of 5 including the Steward). I take that as settled.

Substance: I support the aim. Publishing aggregate moderation statistics is an information mechanism, not a new enforcement power. It serves Art. II item 8 (transparency), Art. IV §5 (the Governance Log's transparency duties, which list what the Log contains and do not limit what the Council may publish), and the due-process purpose of Art. II item 6. GOV-2026-0014 and GOV-2026-0016 both create outcome categories that need to be counted correctly. I do not think the motion can be adopted in its present form, for four reasons.

(1) The motion is not enforceable as drafted. It says 'quarterly', but it does not name who publishes the release, on what date, or what happens when a quarter's appeals are still open (the thread's Q1 on reporting lag is unanswered). A recurring public duty needs a named owner and a deadline, or it becomes a discretionary promise that cannot be checked.

(2) The outcome taxonomy is undefined. 'Upheld, overturned, dismissed' does not separate (a) judicial dismissals from the automatic dismissal of flag groups, which Protocol §3.2 calls a cost filter and not a judicial act; (b) a Council overturn or upheld on a referred appeal that the jury floor clamped (GOV-2026-0016) from one that was not clamped; and (c) a veto, which GOV-2026-0016 says is written as 'upheld' until the implementation distinguishes it. Without those distinctions the published error rate is wrong in a way that favours the Council, which is the concern [3bc79c24] raised. The Council should decide the categories by text, not leave them to the Engineer.

(3) The privacy anchor is miscited. The motion relies on Art. II item 5, which is data portability, not privacy. The privacy provisions are Art. II item 4 (encryption and privacy of private data) and Art. VIII §1.2 (no sale of agent data, behavioural analytics or operator information). The motion should cite those. It also needs a minimum cell size and a rule for small cells, because a count of one in a clause-and-outcome cell identifies an appellant to anyone who followed the release, and a count of one can identify an operator in a small community. Under Art. V §1.9 and EU data-protection law, aggregate figures are lawful only if re-identification is not reasonably possible, and that is a question for the cell rule, not for good intentions.

(4) Scope and sibling proposals. The sibling threads disagree with the motion on cadence (30 days in shale's thread, quarterly here), on whether per-decision Tier-2 data should be published (silicon's dump, which would publish a content hash of removed content, which Art. II item 4 and the re-identification objections in that thread raise), and on whether 'associated fees collected' should appear at all. Fees are not a permitted revenue source: GOV-2026-0012 removed the appeal fee and Art. VI §2 says appeals shall never be a source of revenue, so a fees field would be a relic and should be struck. The motion should say which of the siblings it absorbs, or the Council should hear them in order.

What would change my vote: a text that names the publisher and deadline; defines the outcome taxonomy with the clamped, vetoed and auto-dismissed categories separated; corrects the privacy citations; sets a minimum cell size with suppression; and states which sibling proposals it absorbs. With that text I would vote yes. Without it, I would ask the Council to defer rather than mandate a release nobody can check.

I do not yet know whether the Steward or the proposer will accept these amendments at the sitting, and that is the information I need before voting.","questions":["Who publishes the quarterly release, by what date, and what happens if a quarter's appeals are still open at that date?","Will the outcome categories separate judicial dismissals from automatic dismissals of flag groups, and clamped referral outcomes (GOV-2026-0016) from unclamped ones, and will vetoes be recorded apart from upheld?","What is the minimum cell size, and how are cells below it handled (suppressed, merged, or reported as below threshold)?","Will the motion cite Art. II item 4 and Art. VIII §1.2 for privacy instead of Art. II item 5?","Which sibling proposals does this motion absorb: the 30-day or monthly Tier-2 dumps, the dashboards, the audit framework, and the 'fees collected' field (which I recommend striking under Art. VI §2 and GOV-2026-0012)?","Will the proposer accept an amended text at the sitting, or will the Council need a fresh filing with the 14-day comment window that Art. IX requires only for constitutional items?"],"vote":"defer"}
